_comment: Dependency index for documents that MUST STAY CURRENT. Each entry names the authoritative
sources a document was derived from, and the date it was last checked against them.
Checked by scripts/docs/check_doc_sources.py — when a source changes after a document's
'reviewed' date, that document is flagged as possibly stale. See CORE.md section 5.
DELIBERATELY NOT INDEXED: docs/decisions/, docs/contracts/ and docs/audits/. Those are
point-in-time records and frozen interfaces — they are superseded, never refreshed, so a
staleness flag on them would be noise. See .ai/skills/docs-author/references/DESIGN-DOC.md.
'reviewed' is an attestation ('someone read this against its sources on this date'), not an
edit date. Fixing a typo does not advance it; re-checking the content against the sources does.

docs.note: Sign-in model and roster/auth rules from PROJECT.md; the night-before due date rule from CORE.md section 2, whose HOUR is per-course policy (2359 for both phys-215 and phys-110 as of 2026-08-06) — if a course changes it, this page is wrong; what the Lessons and Dashboard pages actually show from the student modules. The release window became a source on 2026-08-04: schema.js LOOKAHEAD_DAYS is the number this page quotes to students, so changing it makes the page wrong the same day. The Gemini backup joined on 2026-08-19: this page tells cadets a backup link appears when a lesson has one, so backup-builds.json going empty, or backup.html changing what it offers, makes that paragraph wrong.

Student-facing promise about what AI does and does not decide. CORE.md section 6 governs 3-state grading, is_finalized=false, and the hidden diagnostics; the two skills define what actually gets written.

The 3-state toggle, question_scores shape, and the 'all my sections' scoping rule. If the Grade tab's behaviour changes, this doc is wrong before anything else is. nav.js is a source because the page has NO nav entry (P1.14, 2026-07-23) — the doc's 'getting to the Grade page' section is the only place that is written down, so a nav change silently invalidates it. grade.html is a source because the hand-grading queue is rendered there, not in the data module. faculty-tasks.js is a source since 2026-07-27: the due-out boxes are the documented route to this page, and they are now one box per assignment that deep-links into it, so a change to that registry invalidates the 'Getting to the Grade page' section. lessons.html is a source since 2026-07-29: the Assignments page now carries a Grade button that deep-links here, so it is one of the enumerated routes and a change to it invalidates the list. report.html is a source since 2026-08-10: the doc's last section documents the Report tab's two response panels — their controls, their sampling and their selection behaviour — and had been describing that page since it was written with nothing connecting the two, so a change there could never have flagged it. grade-controls.js and schema.js became sources on 2026-08-21, when the page stopped having only one kind of card: grade-controls.js owns BOTH controls the doc describes (the 3-state credit chip and the 0/1/full points toggle), and schema.js's cardKindFor() decides which card each cadet gets — so a change to either alters what an instructor sees without touching faculty-grade.js or grade.html at all.
Says in-page that CORE.md and PROJECT.md remain authoritative and that this page is the bug if they disagree — so it is the entry most likely to need a refresh when the contract moves.
Summarises the shared-state rules and the operating contract. Must never contain what SYSTEM_GUIDE.md may contain — help docs are public at every tier.
The authoring contract. Documents the renderer's actual behaviour — tier gating, the manifest fields, the no-front-matter Jekyll trap. Not served to users.

Course-director and system operating guide. Roles, edge functions, and admin procedures are defined in PROJECT.md and must agree. The two account edge functions are sources because the deploy list here is the ONLY complete one — a function written and not added to it is a function a from-scratch rebuild silently omits, which fails at the moment somebody cannot sign in. log-tutor-error became a source on 2026-08-25: the deploy list in this guide is the only enumeration of what a from-scratch setup must deploy, and it says so -- a function missing from it fails at the point somebody rebuilds the project and cannot tell what is absent. The install step also gained the Windows path that day; it had only ever documented brew, on a project whose machines are Windows.

The ordered PREP v2 cutover procedure. Derived step-for-step from the bootstrap SQL (roles, auth-FK, read window, seal) and the migration script (what moves, what is left behind, the frozen-slug check). If either changes, the runbook is wrong before anything else.

Encodes the help-doc mechanics (no front matter, start at ##, manifest fields, tier gating) and the docs/ taxonomy. If the renderer or the taxonomy changes, the skill teaches the wrong thing to every future author.

Conceptual companion to director-schema-reference.md, which owns the field-level detail and the enforced-rules list; this page links out rather than restating them, after a restated unlock rule drifted and contradicted the reference. Deliberately contains no UI procedures - it explains the model, not the screens, so a page rename cannot invalidate it. (This note used to justify that by saying site/app/ does not read the app schema yet; it has read it since 2026-07-21 - the reason stands, the justification did not.) faculty-lessons.js became a source on 2026-07-28: whether reusing an assignment SHARES it or COPIES it is the content model, not a screen, and it is decided in saveLesson() rather than in any migration - this page said 'schedule the same library entry again instead of copying it', which was true until that day and is now the opposite of what happens. The decision doc is listed beside it because it is where the reasoning lives. schema.js and faculty-lessons.js became sources on 2026-08-04, when publishing stopped meaning 'students can see it': the release window (LOOKAHEAD_DAYS) and the opens_at override are content-model facts, and this page now explains the difference.

Every table and field transcribed from the app-schema migrations and verified against information_schema on the live database. Owns the enforced-rules list and the exact accepted values. Inline SVG depends on the .sf-* classes in styles.css. Omits RLS policy predicates - help docs are world-readable at every tier. SOURCES MUST LIST EVERY MIGRATION: the list stopped at 006 until 2026-07-22, so 007-009 landed without ever flagging this page and analysis_runs went undocumented for two days. Add the new file here whenever a migration is added. ei_sessions states its staff-only access rule in plain language and nothing more: that absence of a student policy is load-bearing (notes may hold a candid read of a cadet), so do not delete the sentence - and do not 'complete' it by pasting the policy SQL either. schema.js became a source on 2026-08-04 — it owns the release window that opens_at overrides, and the is_published row is only correct while that rule is described beside it. LISTING THE MIGRATION IS NOT THE SAME AS ABSORBING IT: 017_due_by_day was in this list from the day it landed, and the page still said three deadline sources and omitted due_by_day from assignment_offerings until 2026-08-10. The flag fired every time; nobody read the doc against the source it named. When this page is flagged, re-read the section the source touches, not just the date. faculty-grade.js and faculty-rollup.js became sources on 2026-08-10: `grades.diagnostic` is free-form jsonb, so its CONTENTS are defined by the code that writes them and by no migration at all — `effort_override` (faculty-grade.js) and `flag_overrides` (faculty-rollup.js) are instructor decisions living in that column, and listing only the migrations would never flag this page when a new key appears in it.

The only documentation of the in-person password-reset workflow, which replaced email recovery on 2026-07-21, and of the registrar roster-export format. If reset-student-password's authorization or the importer's required columns change, this page misdirects an instructor standing in front of a locked-out cadet. Both pages are sources since 2026-07-23 (P1.9): reset lives on Roster and is an instructor action, import and provisioning live on Enrollment and are a director's — the doc sends the reader to one or the other by name, so a move between them makes it wrong. The three staff-password sources were added 2026-07-27, when a derivable default (last name + 1234) made a delegated staff reset possible: this page is now the only place the rule is written down for a human, and the derivation itself has three code copies that must agree.

Defines what a per-language pattern file holds and why these are references rather than skills. CORE.md section 2 is where the read-before-you-code rule lives, and `.ai/README.md` carries the workspace map this directory was added to -- if either moves, this page describes a layout that no longer exists.

Encodes the project's Python version, dependency policy, and the fact that no formatter, linter, type checker, or test framework is installed. The dependency policy is the load-bearing one: CORE.md section 2 decides whether the project is standard-library-only, and an agent reading a stale answer adds an import that breaks a script for the next operator. The `cpp.md` entry was removed at bootstrap along with the file -- this project does not write C++.
Packages work for handoff under the operating contract. CORE section 5 governs git, publish and CHANGELOG, which is the whole surface this skill automates.
The procedure for editing the instruction contracts themselves. CORE.md is both its authority and its most common subject, so a change to CORE's rules changes what a safe change is.
Defines how skills are written and where they live. CORE.md sets the operating rules every skill must respect and `.ai/README.md` defines the directory layout it writes into.

A hand transcription of TABLE 1 (page 10) of the syllabus cadets are issued, and the file scripts/fall2026/set_reading_descriptions.py reads for a lesson's assigned reading -- which it writes into app.assignments.description, where every phys-110 cadet reads it. Added 2026-08-11, the day the syllabus first entered the repo; before that the script reported phys-110 as uncoverable on every run. Registered for the reason its phys-310 sibling was: a transcription that goes stale in silence is this repo's known failure mode. The transcription was verified structurally rather than by re-reading -- all 37 preflight lessons' M/T meeting dates match SCHEDULES['phys-110'] in scripts/fall2026/set_due_dates.py, which was itself checked against site/data/academic-calendar.json, so a dropped row or shifted column would break that agreement. The READING values have no such independent check and are exactly why this entry exists. NOTE the syllabus's Reading column is Cengage SECTION numbers, not the OpenStax PAGE ranges in activities.content.reference_pages; the two are reading-shaped and one column apart. The PDF is binary, so the checker can only compare mtimes -- enough, because any syllabus revision at all warrants re-reading Table 1.

The build skill reads this for a lesson's topic and reading, and scripts/fall2026/set_reading_descriptions.py reads its Reading column into app.assignments.description, where every cadet sees it. Registered 2026-08-11, the day the current syllabus first entered the repo -- and registering it immediately found four wrong readings. The file had described itself as a byte-for-byte unmodified copy of preflight-kit/examples/phys215_fall2026_schedule.md since 2026-08-04; against the syllabus's page-11 table, lesson 3 was missing ', Lab Manual', lesson 5 read 22.5 for 22.6, and lessons 36 and 37 were SHIFTED BY ONE ROW (36 carried lesson 39's '43.8, 43.10'). Only the shift was detectable without the syllabus, and only because it left 36 and 39 duplicated; the other three looked entirely plausible. That is the whole argument for this entry. NOTE the Reading column is CENGAGE section numbers (the book cadets hold) and cannot be mapped mechanically onto the OpenStax text the tutor is grounded in. Two TOPIC strings still disagree with the syllabus (lessons 3 and 16) and are deliberately left alone: topic text is baked into this course's published artifact slugs and matches the live app.assignments titles, so changing one is a republish, not an edit. The kit example still carries all four reading errors and was not corrected -- the kit is never edited per course. The PDF is binary, so the checker can only compare mtimes; enough, because any syllabus revision warrants re-reading the table.

A transcription of what the Lab 1 analysis workbook COMPUTES -- the cell addresses and formulas behind net activity, the per-point uncertainty, the anchored manual fit, the reduced chi-square, and the regression block -- written so the next operator does not have to unzip an xlsx to ground a lesson in it. Registered the day the lab documents entered the repo (2026-08-19) and the Lab 1 artifact was rebuilt against them, because the transcription is load-bearing in the way this repo already knows it can go wrong: the artifact's TEXTBOOK_REFERENCE now states the workbook's uncertainty as a LINEAR SUM of the source and background terms, which is what cell D13 does and is NOT quadrature. The previous build asserted quadrature, from a reconstructed textbook section rather than from the sheet, and would have had a cadet arguing with the spreadsheet in front of them. If the workbook is revised, that claim and the reduced-chi-square/two-thirds pair are the first things to re-read. BOTH sources are binary, so the checker can only compare mtimes -- enough, because any revision to either warrants re-reading the cells.

A hand transcription of the workbook's Schedule sheet, and the file the build skill actually reads for a lesson's topic and reading. Added 2026-08-05 after the transcription went stale in silence: recker updated the workbook, five lessons were renumbered and lesson 2's topic changed from 'Atoms and Nuclei' to 'Energy, Atoms, and Nuclei', and the checker reported every indexed document current because this one was not indexed. The topic string is what this course mints its slug, filename, and component name from, so a stale transcription here does not produce a cosmetic error -- it produces an artifact whose identity disagrees with the schedule, discoverable only by reading both. The workbook is binary, so the checker can only compare mtimes; that is enough, because any workbook edit at all warrants re-reading the sheet.

Restates the prefill-link procedure as a runbook: the base URL, the parameter values, and the slug-match guard. The contract is frozen and authoritative -- if it moves, this page is wrong. BOTH profiles are sources because the two courses deliberately differ on the slug shape (phys-310 carries no lesson number, phys-215 requires one) and on course_id, and this page tells the operator to verify a slug against exactly that convention -- so a slug-rule change in EITHER profile makes this page actively harmful, not merely stale. Added phys-215 on 2026-08-04 when the second course landed. Re-checked 2026-08-14: both profiles gained a `backup_base` endpoint line for the Gemini backup router. That is an endpoint, not a slug rule -- the slug conventions this page depends on are untouched, so the page is still correct.

The capability-scoped path for an artifact AUTHOR, as ONBOARD-AGGREGATION.md is for a close-out operator. Every command it gives is sync_artifacts.py, so that tool's flags and its course-discovery rule are load-bearing: the runbook tells a reader that an unlisted course means a missing COURSE_PROFILE.md, which is true only while discovery reads the local tree. artifact_parse.py is a source because the doc's central promise -- review works on the first push, with no build log written -- rests on objectives being parsed out of the .jsx. faculty-artifacts.js is a source because the doc says the course tab appears after the push, which is true only while the page discovers courses from Storage. patch_artifacts.py and to_gemini.py became sources on 2026-08-20: section 7 now gives the patch-then-port order as four literal commands and states that the porter REFUSES an unpatched source rather than warning about one, and section 1 tells a reader that grep -c BACKUP_ENDPOINT should report 3. Every one of those is a property of a script rather than of this runbook — a reordered step, a relaxed assertion, or a differently named injected constant makes the page wrong with nothing else to catch it.

The one table of what each of the three tutor builds carries -- the kit that emits a new artifact, the 51 published sources, and the 44 Gemini builds -- and the carry-forward backlog for the artifact builder. Written 2026-08-21 after nine changes landed on the Gemini builds in one day and none reached the kit. Every source here is load-bearing in a different way. to_gemini.py owns section 4 verbatim: the two ladders quoted there ARE its LADDER_TEACHING and LADDER_LEGACY constants, so a model name added, dropped or reordered makes that section wrong immediately, and --policy is documented as short-lived so its deletion must delete section 4.4 with it. patch_artifacts.py owns the 2026-08-20 fix-set rows in section 2.1 and the keep-the-slug rule in section 5. The kit SKILL.md and MANIFEST.sha256 are what section 2.2's central claim was measured against -- eleven markers probed, all zero -- so any kit update invalidates that column and is exactly the event this doc exists to be re-read on. The gemini-port skill owns how a build is produced and verified. The data contract owns the submit wire format all three share, and its 3.2 slug rule is what section 5 warns is a rule about a new OFFERING and not about a patch. CORE.md and PROJECT.md carry the no-Node-on-the-deploy-path rule and the sharp-edges table that section 7 restates. Section 3's claim -- that three report-stage hang bugs are still live in the Claude artifact -- was read out of the cached .jsx sources, which are gitignored and cannot be listed as a source here; re-verify it against _builder/courses/*/artifacts/*.jsx rather than trusting this file. patch_tutor_diagnostics.py became a source on 2026-08-25: it owns section 2.3 outright and it is now the only writer of the fix set for the six phys-110 builds that have no .jsx source and cannot be ported -- so a step added or dropped there makes 2.3 wrong for part of the fleet with to_gemini.py unchanged. Section 4 stopped describing a proposal on the same day: --policy teaching is what all 44 builds run.

The publish runbook and the verbatim-reproduction prompt it hands to the publishing session. The prompt enumerates what must not be edited, so it goes wrong the moment the contract's slug rule (section 3.2), endpoint, or codec changes, or the skill's artifact structure does. It also tells the operator to run check_artifact.py and compare a line count -- if that script's invocation or output changes, step 1 and step 3 stop matching what the operator sees. patch_artifacts.py became a source on 2026-08-20, when section 5 (republishing a patched artifact) was written around it and steps 3 and 4 began describing what it injects — the two backup doors, grep -c BACKUP_ENDPOINT reporting 3, the 429 ladder walk, the phase-deferred prompt tail, and the &v=claude marker. It is also the script that asserts byte-equality of the slug line, which is the whole basis of section 5's keep-the-slug rule. stage_for_upload.py joined the same day: section 5 names its output directory, its filename shape and its INDEX.md checklist, so a change to any of those makes the batch-staging paragraph describe something the operator will not find. restamp_build_log.py and sync_artifacts.py joined later on 2026-08-20, after the failure section 5 now warns about actually happened: index.json is REBUILT from BUILD-LOG.md by every push and the stamp written into it was discarded, so the faculty Artifacts page served 51 superseded builds while every source uploaded byte-perfect. The runbook had said to write BUILD-LOG.md first the whole time; what it lacked was the reason and the tool. sync_artifacts.py is a source because that rebuild-from-the-log behaviour, and the fact that `status` compares the rebuilt catalogue against its own stale upload and so cannot detect this, are properties of that script rather than of this page -- change where push reads published_url from, or make status compare something else, and section 5's warning becomes wrong with nothing to catch it.

A FROZEN SNAPSHOT of PREP's own contract, taken 2026-07-30 when preflight-kit was extracted from this project, and hash-locked by _builder/preflight-kit/MANIFEST.sha256. It is deliberately a second copy: the kit is portable and self-contained, and tools/localize.py and tools/verify.py both operate on these files. Registering it here is the mechanism that stops the duplication being silent — a flag means PREP's authoritative copy moved, and the decision is what the kit owes in return. As of the import the two ALREADY differ (data contract by 1 line, prefill link by 35); PREP's is newer, and re-syncing the kit was deliberately not part of the import. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-20, AND THE ANSWER FLIPPED THE SAME DAY IT WAS WRITTEN. This note said earlier on 2026-08-20 that the kit copy was still correct because `an artifact built from the kit does not send v`. That held for hours. The kit's own skill/preflight-factory-v2/SKILL.md is now at rev 5 and teaches emitting `&v=claude` outright, plus `model` and `model_downgraded` inside `d` — so an artifact built from the kit DOES send `v`, and it sends a key the frozen contract sitting beside it in the same seal does not document at all. A downstream port that reads only these contracts would meet that key as output from an unspecified producer. THAT IS NOW A RE-SYNC TRIGGER, and it is PROVENANCE.md's FIRST kind — `a skill or source revision` — not its second. It is NOT a schema:2 event: nothing is renamed, retyped or removed, the four frozen hash keys (t/i/r/d) are untouched, and the payload is still schema 1, so it does not carry the every-deployed-artifact-everywhere weight PROVENANCE reserves for a contract revision. What makes it a trigger is narrower and sufficient: the hash-locked seal now holds two files that contradict each other. SKILL.md was re-synced to rev 5 and the manifest re-sealed around it; the contract beside it was left at the pre-`v` text. The remedy is PROVENANCE's copy-then-regenerate procedure, run as one unit — copy docs/contracts/INTERACTION-DATA-CONTRACT.md over the kit copy, regenerate the MANIFEST.sha256 tail keeping its comment header, then run tools/verify.py — and it needs the course director, because the manifest is the seal and re-sealing is theirs. Until that runs, read the kit copy as one revision behind its own skill, not as a description of what a kit-built artifact sends. Do not 'fix' it by editing the kit copy alone — that breaks MANIFEST.sha256.

Capability-scoped onboarding for a new close-out operator, as distinct from MACHINE-SETUP.md's full development parity. lesson_aggregate.py is a source because this document states what worklist prints and what --as-of does; prep_doctor.py because it reproduces the capability list; check_grounding.py because it quotes the expected 58 of 58.

Was unindexed until 2026-08-07 and had carried a textbook_base_path that resolves zero of 58 manifest entries — precisely the silent rot this index exists to catch. A machine set up from a stale copy of this file is a machine that grades a whole cohort without textbook grounding.

Records BOTH scheduled lesson-cycles: job 1 (Linux box, phys-215, 01:00 nightly, shell wrapper driving claude -p) and job 2 (Windows box, phys-110 + phys-310, 00:33 nightly, a session-only CronCreate prompt fanning out to subagents). The repo deliberately ships no scheduler and CORE.md forbids keeping the fact in agent memory. The two are safe to overlap ONLY because their courses are disjoint — if a course is added to either, check it is not in the other. SKILL.md is a source because this page restates its unattended contract AND corrects it: the documented claude -p "/lesson-cycle" slash form returns "Unknown command" with num_turns=0 and exit 0 on any clone without a .claude/skills/ mirror, which CORE.md section 4 forbids creating. app_tier_check.py and check_grounding.py are sources because both gate tables name them and state what passing looks like; job 2 was missing the grounding gate until 2026-08-10. lesson_aggregate.py is a source because job 2 documents worklist --latest semantics, its offering-wide submissions count, and that pull rejects a bare lesson slug.

The runbook for porting one published Claude artifact to its Gemini backup build. to_gemini.py is the source it most directly describes -- the skill states which transforms run, which assertions refuse rather than warn, and what each refusal means, so a changed transform or a relaxed assertion makes the skill teach the wrong thing. backup.html is a source because the skill documents the router's slug contract and its deliberate lack of auth. The data contract governs the frozen submit surface and the per-offering slug rule (section 3.2) the skill's same-slug guarantee rests on. The factory SKILL.md is a source because it emits the BACKUP_ENDPOINT button the router receives -- if the factory stops emitting it, or emits a different URL shape, the two halves stop meeting and neither one errors.
